title: Religious Identity of Management Teams and Firm Productivity: An Economic Case for Embracing Workplace Diversity
affiliations: Vancouver School of Economics

detail.title: Religious Identity of Management Teams and Firm Productivity: An Economic Case for Embracing Workplace Diversity
detail.abstract: This paper models the trade-off between the creative generation of ideas in a team of managers with diverse religious backgrounds against their discomfort from dealing with colleagues with different religious identities. This is done by operationalizing the important concept of managerial engagement. The paper identifies the features of the optimal religious mix that a secular owner of a competitive firm would choose for the management team. Generally, this optimum entails a tendency towards firm segregation of management by religion. It is seen that competition-especially domestic-entrenches the tendency towards this segregation. Aspects of globalization that would encourage more diversification by religion are identified. The role played by anti-religious discrimination laws in promoting diversity is discussed. It is argued that such laws, by spurring profitable organizational innovation, can be more efficacious in generating religious diversity in private management teams.

title: A Tale of Two Worlds: Exploring the Range and Depth of NGO-Academics Collaboration in International Development across Europe
affiliations: , , University of Vienna, Palacký University Olomouc, Hungarian Academy of Sciences (HAS) - Institute for World Economics,  and Hochschule Bonn-Rhein-Sieg

detail.title: A Tale of Two Worlds: Exploring the Range and Depth of NGO-Academics Collaboration in International Development across Europe
detail.abstract: Studies on NGO-academics collaboration in international development focus on the joint conduction of research, often neglecting other cooperation activities. Here, we inductively explore and catalogue a fuller picture of NGO-academics relations, including practitioner perspectives towards academia. Based on 20 interviews with European development NGO staff and 51 survey responses, we devise a typology to capture the types and purposes of as well as barriers to NGO-academics collaboration and find that joint research conduction is rare. We reason that this is due to the systemic incompatibility of development practice and academic research –known across disciplines as the academic-practitioner divide– and conclude that more collaborative research is unlikely as long as the respective merits systems do not change.

title: The Proof-Execution Gap: A Universal Framework for Computational Veracity in Adversarial Environments

detail.title: The Proof-Execution Gap: A Universal Framework for Computational Veracity in Adversarial Environments
detail.abstract: High-stakes algorithmic industries, ranging from pharmaceutical approval to systematic trading, currently suffer from a structural decoupling between the logic claimed in research (Proof) and the logic deployed in production (Execution). This "Proof-Execution Gap" necessitates a reliance on social trust, leaving systems vulnerable to model drift, p-hacking, and outcome switching. To resolve this, we propose the Computed Veracity Protocol (CVP), a generalpurpose framework that binds Logic, Data, and Environment into an immutable cryptographic tuple. Leveraging hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), the protocol establishes Computational Veracity"-a mechanism allowing third-party Verifiers to mechanically validate that reported outputs originate from a specific, attested logic state without requiring the disclosure of proprietary source code. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a reference implementation in the investment industry, termed the Strategy Validation Package (SVP). By enforcing a mandatory Standardized Test Suite and recording evidence to a tamper-evident transparency log, the protocol mitigates the "Backtest Crisis" and ensures process integrity. Finally, we outline the generalization of these primitives to non-financial domains, including clinical trials and AI governance, providing a unified standard for algorithmic accountability in adversarial environments.

title: Extensions of the Bellman Operator: A Comprehensive Mathematical Treatment
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: Extensions of the Bellman Operator: A Comprehensive Mathematical Treatment
detail.abstract: We provide a rigorous mathematical treatment of extensions to the classical Bellman operator in dynamic programming and reinforcement learning. Beginning with the foundational contraction mapping framework, we systematically develop distributional, risk-sensitive, entropy-regularized, multi-objective, and robust Bellman operators. For each extension, we establish existence and uniqueness of fixed points, characterize convergence rates, and prove essential structural properties. We further analyze the spectral theory of Bellman operators, their connections to semigroup theory and infinitesimal generators, and categorical perspectives that unify diverse extensions. Applications to continuous-time control, partial observability, and mean-field games are developed with complete proofs for the core contractionbased results and with classical proof outlines where standard. This synthesis provides a unified mathematical foundation for modern reinforcement learning theory.

title: Geometric Portfolio Diversification: Wedge Volume, Regime Detection and the Geometric Beta Strategy
affiliations: GeometriX Intelligence and

detail.title: Geometric Portfolio Diversification: Wedge Volume, Regime Detection and the Geometric Beta Strategy
detail.abstract: Modern Portfolio Theory relies on linear correlation to measure diversification, yet this scalar pairwise approach fails to detect high-dimensional collapse-a phenomenon we term the "Risk Pancake." We demonstrate that Geometric Algebra's wedge product provides a superior framework for measuring true portfolio diversification through k-dimensional hyper-volume. Across 21 years and 9 SPDR sector ETFs, our geometric approach produces dramatically more stable regime detection than Hidden Markov Models: nine times fewer switches, ten times fewer false positives, and correctly distinguishes structural collapses from orderly bear markets. Through geometric beta decomposition, we reveal that Energy possesses unique orthogonal energy exceeding the market itself, while cyclical sectors are geometric near-clones despite appearing distinct in traditional metrics. We demonstrate an actionable application: the Geometric Beta Strategy, a rules-based systematic portfolio in the spirit of Smart Beta that allocates to equities during healthy markets, rotates to geometric hedges during stress and moves to cash during structural collapse. Over 16 years, this strategy captured 87% of S&P 500 returns while reducing maximum drawdown, achieving better risk-adjusted performance across all metrics. The geometric approach transforms portfolio diversification from correlation accounting to dimensional geometry, offering practitioners a deterministic alternative to both traditional market-cap weighting and factor-based Smart Beta strategies.

title: Disproving the Lagrange Mathematics in Economics
affiliations: Laissez-Faire Economist

detail.title: Disproving the Lagrange Mathematics in Economics
detail.abstract: If the world is free, you can pursue maximum of your objective at will. But you live in a world of limited resources, so Lagrange Mathematics helps you attain the constrained maximum. This paper proves that, at least sometimes, you don't need any Mathematics or Economics to attain such maximum, and that such maximum is, understandably, not optimal. Perhaps, you have misunderstood the word "free". It does not mean free of charge, but means that you are free to hire any optimal amount of input, as long as you pay the input price (bear in mind that borrowing is also an input). More importantly, output should also be free as per this understanding. Then, you obtain something maximal: surplus or proHit. Perhaps, you have also misunderstood your objective of life.

title: Admissible Information Structures and the Non-Existence of Global Martingale Pricing
affiliations: University of Reading

detail.title: Admissible Information Structures and the Non-Existence of Global Martingale Pricing
detail.abstract: No-arbitrage asset pricing characterizes valuation through the existence of equivalent martingale measures relative to a filtration and a class of admissible trading strategies. In practice, pricing is performed across multiple asset classes driven by economic variables that are only partially spanned by traded instruments, raising a structural question: does there exist a single admissible information structure under which all traded assets can be jointly priced as martingales?. We treat the filtration as an endogenous object constrained by admissibility and time-ordering, rather than as an exogenous primitive. For any finite collection of assets, whenever martingale pricing is feasible under some admissible filtration, it is already feasible under a canonical minimal filtration generated by the asset prices themselves; these pricing-sufficient filtrations are unique up to null sets and stable under restriction and aggregation when a common pricing measure exists. Our main result shows that this local compatibility does not extend globally: with three independent unspanned finite-variation drivers, there need not exist any admissible filtration and equivalent measure under which all assets are jointly martingales. The obstruction is sharp (absent with one driver and compatible pairwise with two) and equivalent to failure of admissible dynamic completeness. We complement the theory with numerical diagnostics based on discrete-time Doob-Meyer decompositions, illustrating how admissible information structures suppress predictable components, while inadmissible filtrations generate systematic predictability.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a task-adjusted, country-specific measure of workers’ exposure to artificial intelligence (AI) across 108 countries. Building on Felten et al. (2021), we adapt the artificial intelligence occupational exposure (AIOE) index to worker-level data from the Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) and extend it globally using comparable surveys and regression-based predictions, covering about 89% of global employment. Accounting for country-specific task structures reveals substantial cross-country heterogeneity: workers in low-income countries exhibit AI exposure levels roughly 0.8 United States (US) standard deviations below those in high-income countries, largely due to differences in within-occupation task content. Regression decompositions attribute most cross-country variation to information and communications technology intensity and human capital. Highincome countries employ the majority of workers in highly AI-exposed occupations, while lowincome countries concentrate in less exposed ones. Using two PIAAC cycles, we document rising AI exposure in high-income countries, driven by shifts in within-occupation tasks rather than employment structure.

detail.title: The Private Enforcer: Algorithmic Deterrence and the Shadow Tax on Insider Trading

publicationDetails.detailsText: Chicago Booth Center for Decision Research (Managerial & Organizational Behavior) Working Paper No. Forthcoming

detail.abstract: Can code deter insider trading more effectively than law? In decentralized markets lacking public enforcement, we identify a novel mechanism of "privatized regulation": predatory algorithms (MEV bots) that impose an immediate, state-dependent penalty on toxic order flow. By solving a coupled HJB-QVI equilibrium between a risk-averse insider and a strategic predator, we demonstrate that the threat of "sandwich attacks" functions as an endogenous "shadow tax" on information. This tax generates a structural "Liquidity Trap"-a safe-harbor region where algorithmic deterrence compels insiders into inaction, effectively replicating a regulatory blackout period without legal intervention. However, we show that this "governance by code" comes at a systemic cost: the strategic interaction amplifies jump risk premiums, generating endogenous fat tails and excess crash risk in asset prices. Our findings suggest that MEV is not merely a transaction cost but a market-based substitute for legal deterrence, replacing the delayed penalties of the SEC with the immediate microstructure costs of volatility.

detail.abstract: The study involved air quality monitoring of Biratnagar, a big industrial city in Southeastern Nepal, in four seasons in 2021. The analysis based on the measurement of the various forms of particulate matter (PM1, PM 2.5, PM 10, and TSP) indicates a cataclysmic change in season. The most polluted period is during winter; the average of 155.2 AQI is unhealthy, but it is dramatically lower than the average in April of 102.6 before the monsoon. The monsoon is a much-needed cleanup, purifying the air by an average of 80 percent to a level of Good AQI of 20.3 in June. Although the highest pollution often occurs on days (around 175) at night in winter with temperature inversions and dead air, there is always a safe window in the day. The air quality is much better between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM, with the cleanest air quality recorded at 2:00 PM when solar heating enables the atmosphere to blow out the pollutants. The paper contrasts the patterns with other cities in South Asia to spot the special status of Biratnagar in the Indo-Gangetic Plain and recommends a multi-cyclic model of management, integrating the regional control of its emissions and special safety measures for high-risk winter evenings to be adopted.

title: It’s About Damn Time: Subjective Time and Habit Formation
affiliations: University of Auckland Business School

detail.title: It’s About Damn Time: Subjective Time and Habit Formation

publicationDetails.detailsText: The University of Auckland Business School Research Paper (forthcoming)
publicationDetails.journalName: The University of Auckland Business School Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
The human experience of time is complex, measured objectively yet experienced subjectively, with further variance between individuals, cultures, social contexts and more. While objective time is represented by clocks and calendars, subjective time reflects the personal and psychological experience of time passing. In marketing research, objective time has received significant attention, whereas subjective time remains largely underexplored. This imbalance has left gaps in understanding how subjective time shapes behaviours, particularly in the context of daily task completion and habit formation. 

This research aims to contribute to marketing literature by offering a new conceptualisation of subjective time perception involving three points of subjective time perception: an anticipation, a reflection and subsequently, a meta-view of an individual’s own subjective time perception. Once this conceptualisation is understood, the research will focus on the relationship between subjective time, task completion, and sustainable habit formation. 

Many routine tasks, such as cleaning, meal preparation, or decluttering, are essential for wellbeing yet there are barriers to action, such as time. Incomplete tasks could lead individuals to experience heightened anxiety, stress, and decreased mental and physical health. Understanding how subjective perception of time is anticipated and reflected upon when engaging in these activities offers an opportunity to overcome these barriers. 

Habit formation is a critical process in creating sustainable behaviours. Existing research discusses influences such as external cues, planning techniques, and motivation, with minimal attention to the influence of subjective time. Habits are formed when repeated behaviours become automatic, supporting both basic survival needs and higher-order activities that contribute to thriving, such as self-care and social engagement. However, forming and maintaining these habits often requires overcoming psychological obstacles. Such obstacles include the perceptions of tasks taking more time and energy than what the person feels they have in that moment. Often, just the thought of time needed to complete a task is enough of a barrier to task completion. Subjective time can be reframed or shaped by marketing messaging to reduce these perceived barriers, individuals may find it easier to develop and maintain beneficial habits that enhance their quality of life as well as the environment. 

From a theoretical perspective, this work contributes to marketing by expanding existing frameworks to include subjective time as a key factor in behavioural change. It offers a new lens through which marketers can design messages and interventions that resonate more deeply with individuals’ lived experiences of time. The practical implications could extend beyond marketing into public health, environmental policy, and wellbeing. 

Overall, this research bridges the gap between subjective time, habit formation, and behavioural change, providing valuable insights for marketers seeking to foster meaningful and lasting improvements in individual and societal wellbeing, while extending the current and minimal knowledge base of subjective time in marketing literature. This research also aims to contribute to the current understanding of subjective time in marketing literature by providing a new conceptualisation through investigating three potential dimensions of subjective time perception (anticipation, reflection, meta-view knowledge) and how this can be used to build habits.

title: Disinformation And Electoral Justice: Democratic Challenges For India In A Globalised Digital Era

detail.title: Disinformation And Electoral Justice: Democratic Challenges For India In A Globalised Digital Era
detail.abstract: This article reviews the increasing problem of disinformation to electoral justice in India. As elections are more influenced by the internet, social media, artificial intelligence, and deepfakes have intensified the digital manipulation of traditional propaganda into mass digital propaganda. The 2019 and 2024 general elections case studies indicate that fake news, communal stories, and AI-based material bend the voter opinion, undermine institutional trust, and pose a threat to democracy. The paper examines the regulatory framework of India, such as the Representation of the People Act, IT Act, IT Rules, and the supervision of the Election Commission, as there are gaps in addressing digital disinformation. The article has also referred international regulations, including the Digital Services Act of the EU, NetzDG of Germany, and the Section 230 of the U.S. Communications Decency Act, and to offer a reform proposal, which involves a focus on legal clarity, transparency in algorithms and ensuring electoral justice and securing democratic practices in India.

title: The African Federation Treaty Framework

detail.title: The African Federation Treaty Framework
detail.abstract:
This document presents the African Federation Treaty Framework (AFTF), a transformative institutional blueprint designed to operationalise socio-economic sovereignty and unity across the African continent. Developed by Africa's Sovereign Development Trust® (ASDT) under the leadership of David Okiki Amayo Jr., the AFTF addresses the historical fragmentation and systemic paradoxes that have hindered Africa's development.

The framework proposes a robust Tripartite System of governance, finance, and defence, anchored by innovative mechanisms such as:

  • The African Sovereign Development Finance Fund (ASDF): A sovereign capital source for generational infrastructure projects.

  • OmniGaza®: A sovereign-grade blockchain platform ensuring algorithmic fidelity and transparency in financial transactions and continental intelligence.

  • The United African Defence Force (UADF): A unified defence structure to guarantee regional peace and security.

  • The African Rare Earth Mineral Fund (AREMF): A mechanism to ensure sovereign control and value retention from Africa's critical natural resources.

This comprehensive document details the constitutional foundation, institutional architecture, financial mechanisms, trade integration strategies, and implementation pathways required to realise a borderless, prosperous, and self-determined African future. It serves as a public record and a call to action for African leaders, policymakers, and stakeholders to unite in building a resilient and sovereign continent.

title: Calibrated Autonomy and the 2026 Business Mediation Ordinance: Rethinking Legal Development in China

detail.title: Calibrated Autonomy and the 2026 Business Mediation Ordinance: Rethinking Legal Development in China
detail.abstract: This article contends that China's 2026 Business Mediation Ordinance signals a new model of legal development—one that is neither a straightforward advance toward the rule of law nor a regression from it. I introduce the concept of "calibrated autonomy": the deliberate creation of semi-autonomous spaces for private dispute resolution, which remain firmly integrated within Party-State oversight through institutional mechanisms. Existing scholarship highlights aspects of this phenomenon but overlooks its core logic: the Party-State designs zones of limited legal independence to serve its interests, while ensuring ultimate control. This dynamic is neither full legal autonomy nor its absence, but a distinct third approach that compels a re-examination of legal transformation in authoritarian regimes.

title: Design and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generative AI Agent for Real-Time WhatsApp Auto-Reply Systems
affiliations: University of Wolverhampton and University of Wolverhampton

detail.title: Design and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generative AI Agent for Real-Time WhatsApp Auto-Reply Systems
detail.abstract: The need for intelligent auto-reply systems that can generate context-aware, customized, and dependable responses in real time has increased due to the growing use of instant messaging services. Hallucinations, a lack of contextual memory, and a poor ability to adjust to different communication styles are common problems with traditional chatbot architectures. The design, implementation, and assessment of a Retrieval-Augmented Generative (RAG) AI agent for real-time WhatsApp auto-reply are presented in this study. In order to produce grounded, human-like responses that represent user-specific tone, vocabulary, and conversational patterns, the suggested approach combines huge language models with historical chat data. The design is divided into three primary phases: answer creation using prompt-augmented large language models, semantic retrieval using vector similarity search, and data indexing and embedding. To facilitate real-time communication, a Python prototype implementation was created and implemented via an Android notification-based interface. Comparing retrievalaugmented context to baseline generative techniques, experimental evaluation shows that it greatly lowers hallucination, improves response relevance, and increases conversational coherence. The findings show that RAG-based architectures provide a workable and scalable alternative for customized message assistants, with possible uses in conversational AI systems, customer service, and individual productivity.

contentFormat.other: United Nations AI Policy Recommendations document (via UNECE WP.6) presented / ratified to 193 UN member states at the annual session in Sept 2023.

detail.abstract:
Products making use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other embedded digital technologies are used widely yet without universally agreed or accepted definitions and under varying regulatory frameworks. Regulatory frameworks are often established prior to the arrival and implementation of new technologies and fast developing new use cases. Hence, they may not be able to cater to the emerging risks posed by these products with embedded AI systems or other digital technologies. Ethical and other societal concerns and negative impacts related to the use of products with embedded AI or other digital technologies continue to be addressed by United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) and other global initiatives. 

Such recommendations represent important complementary factors to consider in conjunction with the recommendations in this document as those concerns are closely related to technical regulation. While this document generally covers products that make use of AI or other embedded digital technologies, products subject to domain-specific regulation may fall out of scope, e.g., specifically the following:


• Self-driving cars and autonomous wheeled vehicles


• Autonomous weapons and other military applications


• Standalone AI software platforms and generative AI not embedded in products Self-driving cars and autonomous wheeled vehicles are covered under separate United Nations regulations. 

In contrast, aerial and submarine vehicles as well as robots are within the scope of this document. The deployment of autonomous weapons and defence products with embedded AI system and other digital technologies falls within national defence and national security strategies and hence are out of scope. Despite not applying from a pure scoping perspective, the recommendations of this document may provide useful content within a defence context. 

In contrast to out-of-scope standalone AI software platform and generative AI, products embedded with such AI systems or other digital technologies fall within the scope of this document.

detail.abstract:
Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have rapidly evolved from a conceptual innovation to a clinically validated platform, most notably demonstrated by the success of mRNA-based vaccines. Beyond infectious disease prevention, mRNA technology is now emerging as a versatile therapeutic modality for cancer, autoimmune diseases, and genetic disorders. Its ability to enable transient, programmable protein expression without genomic integration offers distinct advantages over traditional gene therapy and biologics. This review examines the scientific foundations of mRNA therapeutics, advances in delivery systems, and expanding clinical applications beyond vaccines. We critically assess progress in oncology, immune modulation, and monogenic disease treatment, while addressing current challenges related to stability, delivery, immunogenicity, and manufacturing. Finally, we discuss future directions and the transformative potential of mRNA as a platform technology in precision and personalized medicine.

Keywords: mRNA therapeutics, cancer immunotherapy, autoimmune disease, genetic disorders, lipid nanoparticles, platform technology

detail.abstract: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into mental health and mental well-being care represents a significant shift in psychological support delivery. Millions of users are utilizing these systems despite potential architectural misalignment with therapeutic principles [1]. We propose that GenAI operating as open-loop probabilistic predictors introduce epistemic entropy-ungrounded uncertainty that may increase rather than reduce user confusion. The linguistic coherence and empathetic tone of GenAI can bypass critical evaluation filters, functioning as a "cognitive Trojan horse" [2]. We propose a paradigm shift to a Cognitive Integrated Development Environment (Cognitive IDE) that replaces open-ended generation with constrained transformations, treating the human mind as a "codebase" requiring logical consistency checking. We critically evaluate current mitigation strategies (RAG, CoT prompting, Constitutional AI), demonstrating their limitations in clinical contexts, and argue for epistemic alignment prioritizing uncertainty reduction and agency retention over synthetic empathy. This theoretical framework requires empirical validation before deployment.

detail.abstract: Populist regimes often portray multinational enterprises (MNEs) as foreign threats to national sovereignty, reshaping the institutional context for international investment. Drawing on new institutional economics, we examine how populist hostility influences MNEs; choice between cross-border acquisition and greenfield investment. We develop a contingency view in which acquisitions are the preferred establishment mode under populist institutional pressure, but as host-country intellectual property rights (IPR) protection and firm-level research and development (R&D) intensity increase, this preference weakens and can even be reversed in favor of greenfield investment. We test our hypotheses on a firm-level dataset of nearly 8,000 Chinese foreign direct investment (FDI) projects in 65 countries from 2007 to 2023. Logistic regressions support the proposed relationships, and the results remain robust to alternative measures and an instrumental-variable approach.

detail.abstract: The recent wave of EU and U.S. competition law cases against big tech firms and the proposal and sometimes enactment of new regulatory legislation targeting the same companies have fueled a resurgence of interest in antitrust. To explore these developments, the Journal of Law & Innovation convened a symposium on February 2, 2024, in which leading scholars explored the impact of these new developments.  Concerning theories of liability, Daniel Crane examined new approaches to market definition for digital markets, while Daniel Sokol and Bo Zhou argued in favor of relying on traditional antitrust principles.  Regarding remedies, Herbert Hovenkamp offered a critical look at divestiture, suggesting that courts should turn to such structural remedies only as a last resort. In terms of institutions, William Kovacic favorably discussed the role of the FTC, while Babette Boliek surveyed the burgeoning role of state antitrust enforcement. Together, these contributions offer insights into the design of new analytical approaches and shed new light on how existing remedies and institutions can be adapted to secure competition in a digital context.

title: To Collect or to Purchase? Collaboration Between Manufacturer and E-Commerce Platform on Customization
affiliations: Hefei University of Technology, The School of Management, Hefei University of Technology and Temple University - Department of Statistics, Operations, and Data Science

detail.title: To Collect or to Purchase? Collaboration Between Manufacturer and E-Commerce Platform on Customization

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72501087, 72331004, 72471075, and 72188101], the Base of Introducing Talents of Discipline to Universities for Optimization and Decision-making in the Manufacturing Process of Complex Product (111 projects) [Grant B17014], the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities [Grant JZ2023YQTD0075], and the Projects of International Cooperation and Exchanges NSFC [Grant W2411063]. S. Kumar thanks Temple Center for International Business Education and Research for partially supporting this research.

detail.abstract: Recently, an increasing number of manufacturers have started adopting innovative customer-to-manufacturer (C2M) customization alongside traditional make-to-order (MTO) customization. In this context, manufacturers could collect market data independently or purchase data-driven insights from e-commerce platforms to proactively tailor products. However, firms' crucial decision regarding the data acquisition way is unclear and still being debated in practice. In this regard, although the information systems (IS) literature has studied the benefits of acquiring external insights, firms' choice of data acquisition way and the interplay between the two customization models have not been rigorously analyzed despite their practical importance. Hence, our study fills this critical gap by exploring different data acquisition ways in the context of hybrid customization. Our results show that even when the manufacturer could obtain more informative market data under platform-initiated C2M, the manufacturer should still prefer collecting market data independently rather than purchasing data-driven insights. This happens when the marginal cost of data acquisition is high for both the manufacturer and the e-commerce platform, and customers have a stronger bias against the tailored product. This is because these two factors would cause a decrease in data value, diminishing the e-commerce platformąŕs role in data collection. We also find that even when the e-commerce platformąŕs data-driven insights could lead to a higher customization level, which generates more commission revenue, the e-commerce platform should not always provide insight support. Moreover, manufacturercollected C2M may sometimes lead to a higher effort level of acquiring informative data compared to platform-initiated C2M. Further, interestingly, even when the effort level is lower, manufacturer-collected C2M may occasionally result in more customer welfare. These results provide valuable guidelines to manufacturers on choosing an appropriate data acquisition way, to e-commerce platforms on offering data-driven insights, and to policymakers on improving customer welfare. These results also contribute to the emerging literature in IS and related disciplines on data-driven production models.

detail.abstract: This study investigates how anti-corruption efforts influence corporate cash holdings in China, using a novel text-based proxy derived from Party newspaper articles. Contrary to prior studies suggesting anti-corruption increases precautionary cash reserves due to political uncertainty, we find intensified anti-corruption environments reduce cash holdings. Firms no longer need cash for informal payments or political insurance, reallocating funds toward productive investments and shareholder distributions. Private firms and SOEs experience greater declines than central SOEs. Compared to traditional proxies, our Party-newspaper-based measure retains significance after accounting for endogeneity from political uncertainty, while traditional proxies lose explanatory power. By isolating political environment from political turnover, this paper highlights how informal institutions shape corporate financial policy. Our findings contribute to debates on institutional integrity’s role in corporate governance and liquidity management, with implications for firms in environments with weak rule of law or pervasive corruption.

detail.abstract: This paper establishes a rigorous axiomatic framework for the "Organizational Thermodynamics" series (Shoji, 2026a-h), synthesizing the "Organizational Battery Theory" and the "Grand Unified Equation" into a cohesive physicaleconomic system. Moving beyond the neoclassical abstraction of the firm, we define the organization as a Dissipative Structure operating within a multidimensional resource manifold. We derive the "Extended Walrasian Identity" to formalize the intertemporal transfer of market disequilibrium and introduce the "Total Differential of Organizational Potential" using Gibbs free energy. Furthermore, we propose a dimensionless "Canonical Efficiency Function" derived from information-theoretic constraints. This framework mathematically demonstrates that organizational sustainability is not a deterministic function of capital accumulation but a stochastic trajectory selection governed by the Schrödinger Condition, where the entropic boundary supersedes the inflationary boundary proposed by Modern Monetary Theory (MMT).

detail.title: AI ROI Analysis: Evidence from 200 B2B Deployments (2022-2025)
detail.abstract: This working paper presents a comprehensive analysis of Return on Investment (ROI) from 200 artificial intelligence (AI) projects deployed in French B2B companies between 2022 and 2025. Using structured data collection methods including CRM exports, quarterly interviews, and financial audits, we document a conservative Median ROI of +159.8% over 24 months (while unadjusted Mean reached +347% driven by outliers), with an 8-month breakeven period and a 27% failure rate. Our findings challenge common assumptions about AI implementation: contrary to conventional wisdom, projects with smaller initial budgets (<€15K) achieved 2.1x higher ROI than large-scale deployments. We identify five critical success factors including Human-in-the-Loop governance (4.2x fewer critical incidents) and training investment (25%+ of budget = 2.1x ROI multiplier). This research provides evidence-based benchmarks for practitioners and contributes to the emerging literature on AI adoption in mid-sized enterprises

title: Neutral Ratings as Implicit Negative Signals in Online Consumer Reviews

detail.title: Neutral Ratings as Implicit Negative Signals in Online Consumer Reviews
detail.abstract: Research on online customer reviews usually defines rating valence on a positive–negative scale. In doing so, neutral ratings are often treated as the absence of evaluative information. Despite this assumption influencing how online reviews are modelled and interpreted, it is rarely questioned. In this study, we challenge this view and argue that neutral ratings are not behaviourally neutral. Instead, they function as implicit negative signals that influence market outcomes. This article examines the impact of neutral rating scores on online purchases, considering how product category (search vs. experience) and the initial number of reviews (low vs. high) moderate this effect, using a Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) model. We use longitudinal panel data from Amazon to examine the effects of neutral ratings on product sales rank. The results show that neutral ratings have a statistically and economically significant negative effect on sales performance. This effect differs from, and in some cases is stronger than, the effects of positive and negative ratings. In addition, the impact of neutral ratings depends on the information environment. The negative effect is stronger when review volume is low and weaker when the product is a search product. The findings suggest that assuming neutral ratings as analytically neutral can lead to misleading conclusions about the influence of online customer reviews. Therefore, this study calls for reconsidering the way of conceptualization and operationalization of neutrality in research on online customer reviews, with implications for theory, empirical modelling, and platform design.

title: The Psychology of Fee Disclosure: How Drip Pricing Violates Fairness Norms and Undermines Consumer Trust in E-Commerce Checkout Interfaces

detail.title: The Psychology of Fee Disclosure: How Drip Pricing Violates Fairness Norms and Undermines Consumer Trust in E-Commerce Checkout Interfaces
detail.abstract: Drawing on dual entitlement theory (Kahneman, Knetsch, & Thaler, 1986) and mental accounting principles (Thaler, 1985), this research examines how fee presentation formats affect consumer perceptions of price fairness in e-commerce checkout environments. An online experiment with 467 US consumers compared three pricing approaches: all-in pricing (fees included), drip pricing (fees revealed at checkout), and transparent pricing (fees displayed upfront). Results demonstrate that pricing format significantly affects perceived fairness (F(2,464) = 19.10, p < .001, d = 0.70). Critically, drip pricing was rated below the scale midpoint (M = 3.87), indicating consumers perceive it as unfair rather than merely less favorable. All-in pricing (M = 5.03) outperformed both alternatives. Notably, 67–75% of participants expected additional fees, yet drip pricing was still judged unfair—suggesting that expectation does not neutralize negative fairness perception. These findings provide empirical support for the FTC's Junk Fees Rule (2024) and the TICKET Act (H.R. 3950), demonstrating that fee presentation operates as a psychological mechanism that can violate consumers' reference price expectations and fairness norms in digital commerce environments.

detail.abstract: Contemporary research on giftedness has predominantly focused on early cognitive acceleration, high intellectual performance, and advanced symbolic capacities, treating giftedness as an individual trait measurable through psychometric instruments. While this approach has yielded substantial empirical insights, it remains limited in explaining the variability of adaptive outcomes observed in gifted children across different social and institutional contexts. This article advances a systemic conceptualization of giftedness as a sensitivity-based mode of neurocognitive functioning emerging at the intersection of accelerated plasticity and heightened contextual responsivity. Rather than framing giftedness as a linear advantage or a stable personal attribute, the proposed model conceptualizes it as a dynamic regulatory configuration that amplifies both learning potential and environmental load. Drawing on interdisciplinary findings from developmental neuroscience, systems psychology, and regulatory theory, the paper examines how accelerated neural integration and predictive processing capacities increase susceptibility to contextual inconsistency, particularly within standardized early-childhood institutions. Under conditions of environmental mismatch, gifted children may demonstrate transient functional reorganization, including temporary reduction in previously established skills, increased autonomic reactivity, or shifts in behavioral strategies, without evidence of structural impairment. The model reframes such phenomena not as pathological regression but as adaptive regulatory responses aimed at load redistribution and restoration of system predictability. Observational evidence indicates that when environmental parameters regain coherence and relational stability, functional restoration often occurs rapidly and without targeted remediation. By distinguishing cognitive autonomy from emotional-regulatory dependence, the article highlights a critical source of misinterpretation in both educational and clinical settings, where early cognitive maturity is frequently conflated with global self-regulatory capacity. The analysis underscores the necessity of context-sensitive institutional designs capable of accommodating high-plasticity systems without suppressing complexity or inducing defensive reorganization. The proposed framework contributes to a more nuanced understanding of giftedness as a systemic phenomenon with direct implications for educational policy, early-childhood institutional design, and interdisciplinary assessment models. It supports a shift from corrective interventions toward environmental calibration strategies that preserve adaptive potential while maintaining regulatory stability.

detail.abstract: We study the e!ect of licensing-induced, occupation-specific education requirements on workers' occupational mobility and earnings. We study this question in the context of Certified Public Accountants' (CPAs) licensing rules, exploiting the staggered introduction of a change in the number and composition of CPAs' educational requirements across states. We find that an increase in mandatory accounting-specific credit hours leads to more time spent in accounting jobs, less cross-occupation job switching, and a reduction in the licensing earnings premium. Supplemental analyses indicate that the e!ects represent a specialization of worker skills rather than a general decline in CPAs' accounting performance. The collective findings suggest that by imposing occupationspecific course requirements, licensing regimes can create less portable human capital, reducing both occupational mobility and the licensing earnings premium.

detail.abstract: This study uses a choice-based conjoint experiment to estimate consumer willingness to pay (WTP) for hotel sustainability initiatives when booking hotels through online travel agencies in the economy, midscale, and upscale segments. We further characterize the impact of sustainability initiatives on hotel choice probabilities, conditional on price. We find that marginal WTP for hotel sustainability levels is similar in magnitude to that of other conventional hotel attributes such as guest review scores and proximity to destination, despite sustainability being self-reported as relatively less important. Although we find an increase in WTP for sustainability moving from the economy to the midscale segment, there is no significant difference in WTP between midscale and upscale segments, suggesting that the perceived value of sustainability plateaus in the midscale segment. We also collect data on demographics, pro-environmental attitudes, and preferences for sustainability filters when searching for hotels online. We find that stronger pro-environmental attitudes and preferences for sustainability filters are positively correlated with WTP, while demographic characteristics explain relatively little variation in sustainability valuation. Hotel managers can use these findings to identify revenue opportunities that justify investments in sustainability initiatives, better target sustainability messaging, and more effectively position sustainability attributes in online booking environments.

title: Monetary Policy Effects on Firms’ Uncertainty

detail.title: Monetary Policy Effects on Firms’ Uncertainty

detail.abstract: We study how monetary policy affects inflation uncertainty. Using a survey of Mexican firms and exploiting quasi-random variation in the response date, we estimate the effect of a monetary policy decision and surprise on firms’ perceived inflation uncertainty. We find that a one percentage point contractionary monetary policy reduces inflation uncertainty by 0.02 percentage points. We explore how this result is affected by levels of higher and lower aggregate uncertainty. We find that monetary policy tightening is twice as effective in reducing inflation uncertainty in periods of higher economic uncertainty, such as trade uncertainty. Our findings highlight the role of monetary policy in reducing inflation uncertainty. We discuss that in periods of uncertainty, monetary authorities face a trade-off between stimulating the economy and increasing uncertainty about the inflation outlook.

detail.abstract: Political crises often coincide with fiscal crises, with complex causal dynamics at play. We examine the interaction between tax revolts and sovereign risk using a quantitative structural model calibrated to Argentina. In the model, the government can be controlled by political parties with different preferences for redistribution. Households may opt to revolt in response to the fiscal decisions of the ruler. While revolts entail economic costs, they also increase the likelihood of political turnover. Our model mirrors the data by generating political crises concurrent with fiscal turmoil. Specifically, we find that our model aligns closely with the conditions observed during the Macri administration (2015-2019). We find that left-leaning parties are more prone to default upon entering office, while right-leaning parties issue more debt. Our framework explains the high deficits observed during the Macri administration as well as the sovereign default that occurred immediately after the left regained power.

title: Reaching for Yield? Artificial Intelligence and Mortgage Credit Allocation
affiliations: University of Groningen, Faculty of Economics and Business, Students

detail.title: Reaching for Yield? Artificial Intelligence and Mortgage Credit Allocation
detail.abstract: This paper examines how artificial intelligence adoption by U.S. banks affects mortgage lending. Using a novel disclosure-based measure of AI adoption from 10-K filings, I find that AI banks exhibit higher approval rates, charge higher interest rates, and disproportionately expand credit to borrowers with the highest debt-to-income (DTI) ratios-the riskiest segment of the distribution. This pattern constitutes reaching for yield: AI banks extend credit precisely where traditional underwriting is most restrictive. Crucially, despite lending more to high-DTI borrowers, AI banks do not experience higher non-performing loan ratios. These findings suggest that AI improves screening precision, enabling banks to identify creditworthy borrowers within observably risky categories and profitably serve segments previously rationed by conventional underwriting.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the disconnect between falling agricultural commodity prices and persistent food inflation by applying a Heterogeneous Vector Autoregression (VAR) model to a panel of 203 countries using data from 1961 to 2022. It analyzes the impact of global crops, fertilizer, and oil prices on domestic inflation and explores the asymmetries in the pass-through of global shocks. Results show that fertilizer price shocks significantly influence crop pr ices, es pecially maize and soybeans, while production shocks have a weaker effect. Demand-driven price changes exhibit higher pass-through to food inflation compared to supply-driven shocks, with country-specific characteristics shaping these responses. A historical decomposition reveals that global factors played a larger role in inflation during 2021, particularly for emerging economies, while advanced economies were more affected by domestic shocks. These findings highlight the importance of tailored policies to mitigate inflation in the face of global commodity price volatility.

title: A Macroprudential Theory of Foreign Reserve Accumulation

detail.abstract: We propose a macroprudential theory of foreign reserve accumulation that can rationalize the secular trends in public and private international capital flows. In middle-income countries, the increase in international reserves has been associated with elevated private capital inflows, both in the aggregate and in the cross-section, and economies with a more open capital account have accumulated more reserves. We present an open economy model of financial crises that is consistent with these features. We show that optimal reserve management policy leans against the wind, raising gross private borrowing while improving the net foreign asset position and reducing exposure to crises.

title: Exploring the impact of mining on adverse birth outcomes: a scoping review protocol

detail.title: Exploring the impact of mining on adverse birth outcomes: a scoping review protocol
detail.abstract: The objective of this protocol is to guide the conduct of a scoping review that aims at mapping the current knowledge on the links between environmental exposure to mining and adverse birth outcomes. Mining operations can expose pregnant women to a number of environmental health hazards that can affect their pregnancy, and potentially increase their risk of developing ABOs. Identifying and mapping the current evidence on the links between mining and ABOs can inform decision-makers and health practitioners and contribute to the reduction of the toll of ABOs. To our knowledge, a scoping review related to the topic is still not available, and the pertinent literature remains scattered. The review will include all studies that investigate the links between maternal environmental exposures related to mining and ABOs. Only papers published in English and Spanish will be considered. Studies reporting on maternal occupational exposures and non-human studies will be excluded.A systematic search will be conducted in PubMed, and the Web of Science.The details and key findings of the selected studies will be charted and then summarized and presented in both qualitative and quantitative manners.A stakeholder consultation will follow to further discuss the findings and gain additional insights.

detail.abstract: The rapid and correlated ascent of two technologies in public markets—limit-order- books and high frequency trading–make it increasingly unclear what constitutes an “informed trader”, and what, if anything, informed trading has to do with fundamental value and market efficiency. Bitcoin, lacking fundamentals in the traditional cash-flow sense, represents a highly-liquid laboratory, which can help researchers isolate how, and under what time horizons, differing asset pricing valuation mechanisms are impounded in a high frequency world. To this end, I leverage a high frequency cryptocurrency data provider in order to establish some cross-sectional and time series empirical microstructure facts about Bitcoin. First, I study the “term structure of realized spreads” in Bitcoin and find that adverse selection risk to liquidity provision is no longer compensated for, on average, less than 15 seconds for the least voluminous exchange I study, and less than 6 milliseconds for the most voluminous exchange I study. Second, a vector autoregression (VAR) approach suggests that the price impact of net volume of 10,000 Bitcoins is 4.69% at 5 second frequency, 4.91% at 15 second frequency, 4.63% at 1 minute frequency, and 4.44% at the 5 minute frequency. Cross-sectionally, this is significantly larger than equities and ETFs as a percentage of market cap. The cross-sectional heterogeneity in price impact and realized spreads across assets lends early credence to the idea that fundamental valuation differences are still impounded at the microstructural level.

detail.abstract: Motivated by the dominant role of the US dollar, we explore how monetary policy (MP) shocks in the US can affect a small open economy through the expectation channel. We combine data from a panel survey of firms’ expectations in Uruguay with granular information about firms’ debt position. We show that a contractionary MP shock in the United States reduces firms’ inflation and cost expectations in Uruguay. This result contrasts with the effect of this shock on the Uruguayan economy. We study mechanisms related to how firms and managers’ experience in different monetary policy regimes can explain the results and discuss their implications.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we revisit the scope for macroprudential policy in production economies with pecuniary externalities and collateral constraints. We study competitive equilibria and constrained-efficient equilibria and examine the extent to which the gap between the two depends on the production structure and the policy instruments available to the planner. We argue that macroprudential policy is desirable regardless of whether the competitive equilibrium features more or less borrowing than the constrained-efficient equilibrium. In our quantitative analysis, macroprudential taxes on borrowing turn out to be larger when the government has access to ex-post stabilization policies.

detail.abstract: Water scarcity is a problem likely to become more prevalent in many areas of the world in the near future. Changing water pricing schemes such that households' water demand is reduced could be one policy to address the problem. With water demand of households being price inelastic, such an approach, however, would likely require substantial price increases to reduce water demand. We propose an alternative pricing scheme based on the issuance of water-use rights (permits) to households at prices that cover a water supplier's costs. These permits can be traded at the end of the year, where households in excess of permits are redeemed, and households in need of additional permits have to purchase permits. We show that, in such a setting, opportunity cost considerations of households can curtail water consumption and yield lower water bills than a policy that increases volumetric rates.

detail.abstract: We design an experiment to model the decision to self-manage or delegate an investment task. Participants both construct a self-chosen portfolio and choose between it and a delegated alternative. We find that simply asking participants to construct the self-chosen portfolio before presenting a delegated alternative makes them 20 percentage points more likely to prefer the self-chosen portfolio. The composition of the delegated portfolio has no effect on the preference between portfolios, but when presented first it strongly influences the composition of the self-chosen portfolio. Participants who prefer their self-chosen-portfolio also exhibit a greater appetite for risk in constructing that portfolio.

title: A Tale of Two Premiums: How Belief Disagreement Twists the Term Structure of Convenience Yield
affiliations: and

detail.title: A Tale of Two Premiums: How Belief Disagreement Twists the Term Structure of Convenience Yield
detail.abstract: We introduce a novel, high-frequency measure of belief disagreement derived from blockchainbased prediction markets (Polymarket) to investigate the determinants of the U.S. Treasury convenience yield. Unlike traditional volatility indices (VIX) or news-based proxies (EPU), our measure captures "skin-in-the-game" divergence in trader beliefs regarding specific political outcomes. We document a striking asymmetry in how political disagreement affects the demand for safe assets across the maturity spectrum. Shocks to political disagreement significantly compress the convenience yield on short-term Treasury bills, consistent with operational risk and liquidity deterioration, while simultaneously expanding the premium on longterm bonds, reflecting a "flight-to-safety" motive. Our findings demonstrate that political discord generates a "twist" in the safe asset curve-acting as a liquidity shock in the near term but a safety trigger in the long run-and highlight the utility of prediction markets in isolating ex-ante uncertainty from media attention.

title: How Employment Framing Affects Trade Preferences: Evidence from Survey Experiments
affiliations: Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), Inter-American Development Bank and Inter-American Development Bank (IDB)

detail.title: How Employment Framing Affects Trade Preferences: Evidence from Survey Experiments

publicationDetails.journalName: Inter-American Development Bank Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: International trade increases aggregate welfare but also creates winners and losers, which makes free trade a contentious political issue. Recent research has established that individuals are more sensitive to anti-trade information about the prospect of employment loss than to pro-trade information regarding lower product prices and increased variety. This means that we know what works to decrease support for trade, but it is still unclear what works to increase it. In this paper, we fill this gap by studying how individual attitudes and beliefs change in response to information regarding employment losses (in import-competing sectors), to information regarding employment gains (in export-oriented sectors), and to information regarding the possibility of compensation to those displaced by trade. To this end, we conducted a large-scale survey experiment in 18 Latin American countries using nationally representative samples. Results indicate that anti-trade information reduces support for trade even if compensation to losers is mentioned and that pro-trade messages increase support only if they are worded so that a job gain is perceived. Belief updating about the consequences of increased trade on employment seems to be a relevant mechanism. Our findings have important implications on what types of messaging work to increase support for trade.

title: Autoregressive Models with Non-Causal ARCH Volatility
affiliations: Aarhus University - School of Business and Social Sciences and

detail.title: Autoregressive Models with Non-Causal ARCH Volatility
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-causal (forward-looking) ARCH specification in which conditional heteroskedasticity depends on leads of the process. When observed in calendar time, this time inversion allows large past shocks to affect the entire conditional distribution rather than only its scale, as in standard ARCH models. The resulting forward-looking dynamics can generate symmetric bimodal predictive densities, providing a new interpretation of high-volatility regimes. We establish the stochastic properties of autoregressive processes with errors following the proposed non-causal ARCH specification and derive sufficient conditions for consistency and asymptotic normality of an Approximate Quasi-Maximum Likelihood Estimator (AQMLE). A kernel-based estimator of the marginal error distribution and the predictive density is also developed. Simulation results demonstrate good finite-sample performance. An empirical application to monthly CPI data shows that the proposed model captures distributional dynamics more effectively than traditional approaches, particularly during periods of elevated uncertainty and volatility.

title: A Critique of Republic Act No. 11058: The Occupational Safety and Health Standards Law
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Unaffiliated Authors

detail.title: A Critique of Republic Act No. 11058: The Occupational Safety and Health Standards Law
detail.abstract: Workplace safety is an important concern for many workers in the Philippines. Republic Act No. 11058, also known as the Occupational Safety and Health Standards Law, was created to protect workers from accidents, injuries, and health risks in the workplace. This critique examines the purpose, strengths, weaknesses, and overall impact of the law. The study discusses how the law helps promote safer working conditions by requiring employers to provide safety training, protective equipment, and information about workplace hazards. However, it also highlights problems in implementation, especially among small businesses and due to limited inspections. Although the law has helped increase awareness of workplace safety, its effectiveness depends on proper enforcement and cooperation among employers, workers, and the government. Overall, Republic Act No. 11058 is an important step toward improving labor conditions, but stronger implementation is needed to fully achieve its goals.

title: Protecting the Rights of Internally Displaced persons in the Conflicts in the English Speaking Parts of Cameroon

detail.title: Protecting the Rights of Internally Displaced persons in the Conflicts in the English Speaking Parts of Cameroon
detail.abstract: The protracted armed conflict in Cameroon's English-speaking NorthWest and SouthWest regions has, since 2016, generated a large population of internally displaced persons (IDPs), most of whom are women and children. Forced to flee their homes and livelihoods, these IDPs face severe humanitarian, social, and economic challenges within host communities already marked by poverty and limited access to basic services. This article critically examines the protection afforded to internally displaced persons in the context of the Anglophone crisis, with a particular focus on measures adopted by the Cameroonian State and its partners. Anchored in the triple-pronged theory of state obligations to respect, protect, and fulfil human rights, the study argues that IDPs are entitled to enjoy their rights on an equal basis with other citizens, especially in situations of vulnerability arising from armed conflict. Using a doctrinal and descriptive approach, the article analyses key state initiatives, including the reconstruction process, the Major National Dialogue, peace and reconciliation efforts, the establishment of institutions such as the National Commission for the Promotion of Bilingualism and Multiculturalism and the Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration Committee, as well as social, economic, and health-related interventions aimed at alleviating the plight of IDPs. It further assesses collaborative efforts with humanitarian actors and non-governmental organizations under frameworks such as the Humanitarian Response Plan. The article finds that while notable measures have been adopted, implementation gaps, limited coverage, and sustainability challenges continue to undermine effective protection. It concludes by underscoring the need for more coherent, adequately resourced, and rights-based responses to ensure durable solutions for internally displaced persons in Cameroon's conflict-affected regions.

title: Pension Schemes, Healthcare Use, and Health: Evidence from China

detail.title: Pension Schemes, Healthcare Use, and Health: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: Using a non-parametric fuzzy regression discontinuity design and leveraging data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), this paper explores the impact of public and private pension schemes on health service utilization and health outcomes among urban and rural individuals in China. Our estimates show that receipt of public pensions, particularly the Urban Employee Pension Scheme (UEPS) and Public Employee Pension Scheme (PEPS), significantly improves selfreported health, mental health (CES-D scores), and physical health (ADL scales), especially among urban males who are married and educated. However, there are no significant effects on healthcare utilization among urban people. Similarly, private pension schemes have positive impacts on health outcomes. Moreover, social pensions, the New Rural Pension Scheme (NRPS), increase healthcare utilization (inpatient/outpatient) and corresponding healthcare spending of the rural population, particularly among married and low-educated male residents. Specifically, in urban China, public pension (UEPS/PEPS) receipts have two spillover effects: spousal and inter-generational. These effects manifest in terms of health improvements, intergenerational care, and intra-family transfers. These findings exhibit heterogeneity across gender, rural-urban differences, hukou status, and marital status. Additionally, the health effects stemming from urban pension schemes can be explained by retirement, providing more leisure time for males and grandparental childcare responsibilities for females. However, the positive effect on healthcare use of rural males and the null effect for rural females are driven by the pure income effect of household joint financial pooling under the NRPS and female altruism. Finally, we find that integrating NRPS and URPS increased migration, non-agricultural employment, and health of nonpensioners, with no effect on rural pensioners.

detail.abstract:
The integration of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) into innovation processes remains, in many contexts, partial, instrumental, or primarily driven by funding eligibility and reporting requirements, rather than being systematically embedded in governance structures and decision-making practices. This limitation is particularly evident in territories whose innovation ecosystems depend heavily on public resources and simultaneously face significant socio-environmental challenges, such as the Canary Islands.

This Master’s thesis develops a methodological proposal for integrating CSR into the management and governance of innovation centers and departments, using the public–private innovation ecosystem of the Canary Islands as a reference framework. The study adopts a qualitative research approach based on a review of academic literature on CSR, sustainable innovation, and performance assessment; an analysis of established reference frameworks (ISO 26000, GRI, and the Sustainable Development Goals); and an examination of the European sustainability regulatory framework (CSRD and ESRS), which is employed as a conceptual translation tool rather than as a compliance-oriented scheme.

The outcome is a modular methodology structured around economic, social, environmental, and governance dimensions, designed to embed sustainability criteria into standard processes for the evaluation, support, and design of innovative projects. The proposal includes a set of operational instruments—diagnostic matrices, project templates, monitoring indicators, and continuous improvement mechanisms—intended to support decision-making, organizational learning, and coherence between innovation activities, sustainability objectives, and territorial conditions.

Rather than assessing an implemented pilot, this research offers an applicable and adaptable methodological guide, relevant not only to the Canary Islands innovation ecosystem but also to other contexts in which CSR has yet to be systematically integrated into innovation management practices.

detail.abstract:
The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, awarded for the development of Metal–Organic Frameworks (MOFs), crystallized a paradigm shift in materials science: from the optimization of dense matter to the deliberate design of void space. This work proposes that the mammalian interstitium can be coherently re-described within this paradigm as a naturally occurring, dynamic analogue of a MOF—a “Living MOF”—characterized by hierarchical porosity, self-similar connectivity, and reversible structural plasticity.

Integrating concepts from reticular chemistry with our previously proposed Bio-Topology framework, we argue that the primary functional role of the interstitium is not passive filling but the maximization of mass and entropy transfer through topological connectivity. Within this view, physiological efficiency is governed less by individual vessel geometry than by the global connectivity of a fractal interstitial pore network, which may be quantified in topological terms such as the effective first Betti number.

We further propose that chronic pathological states may be reinterpreted as a topological phase transition of this Living MOF. Under sustained thermodynamic, chemical, or mechanical stress, the interstitial gel may undergo a volume phase transition, leading to hierarchical pore collapse, loss of connectivity, and the emergence of a densified, poorly dissipative “Shadow Phase.” This phase is hypothesized to be largely invisible to conventional macroscopic imaging modalities, despite its systemic physiological consequences.

 Within this conceptual framework, Interstitial Hydrodynamic Modulation (IHM) is interpreted not as an informational or biochemical intervention, but as a macro-scale physical catalyst capable of lowering the activation barrier between metastable topological states. By mechanically re-opening collapsed interstitial pathways, IHM may restore the MOF-like architecture of the biological ground, providing a unified physical interpretation for the apparent reversibility of certain degenerative and chronic conditions.

This paper does not seek to replace existing molecular or clinical descriptions of disease, but to complement them by introducing a mesoscopic, topological layer of description. By reframing the interstitium as a Living MOF, we aim to shift medical physics from an anatomy of solids toward a physics of the void, in which health and disease emerge as distinct topological states of a dissipative biological ground.

title: Common-knowledge Coordination Signals (CKCS): A State-variable Reframe For Multi-agent Stability
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Common-knowledge Coordination Signals (CKCS): A State-variable Reframe For Multi-agent Stability
detail.abstract: Persistent coordination failures-from AI misalignment to institutional paralysis-are often misdiagnosed as communication or incentive problems. This paper proposes they stem from failures of a shared interpretive state governing how agents access and constrain meaning. We introduce Common-Knowledge Coordination Signals (CKCS), a minimal coordination primitive that induces regime transitions from high-variance divergence to low-variance convergence in synthetic multi-agent systems-without modifying agent preferences, incentives, or capabilities. The contribution reframes coordination not as a social challenge but as a state-management problem, aligning with historical cases where identifying governing state variables resolved previously intractable failures. Formal definitions, falsification criteria, and synthetic validation results are provided in the full paper.

title: A General Theory of Process: Unifying Physics, Intelligence, and Topology via Structural Isomorphism

detail.title: A General Theory of Process: Unifying Physics, Intelligence, and Topology via Structural Isomorphism
detail.abstract: Modern science is currently fragmented into siloed disciplines-quantum mechanics, artificial intelligence, network science, and signal processing-each describing complex systems using disparate vocabularies. This manuscript proposes a general theory of process, asserting that these fields are not merely analogous but are topologically isomorphic. By synthesizing fifteen foundational studies, we identify six rigorous structural isomorphisms that map the mechanics of reality across substrates. We demonstrate that the collapse of a wavefunction, the digitization of a signal, and the hallucination of an AI are identical symmetry-breaking events occurring at a bandwidth horizon. We unify the concept of holographic wet hair with anyon density halos and non-Markovian noise, proving that information lost locally is rigorously conserved non-locally. Finally, we propose that computation is not symbolic manipulation but Hamiltonian instantiation, where the arrow of time is generated by the dissipative viscosity required for epistemic stability. This framework provides a Rosetta Stone for interdisciplinary science, translating the physics of the vacuum into the engineering of intelligence.

title: Market-Implied Time to Transition to a Low-Carbon Economy from the Greenium Term Structure
affiliations: University of Milan, , Department of Statistics and Quantitative Methods University of Milano-Bicocca and University of Parma

detail.title: Market-Implied Time to Transition to a Low-Carbon Economy from the Greenium Term Structure
detail.abstract: In the context of the transition to a low or zero carbon economy, we expect the difference in greenium between pairs of twin bonds with different maturities to disappear or, at least, to reduce in both level and volatility. Consequently, we need a model that imposes a terminal condition on the dynamics of the process representing the difference in nodes within the greenium term structure. An important feature of this difference, observed in empirical data, is its mean-reverting behavior. This characteristic motivates the introduction of ad-hoc models that consider the possibility of a transition occurring at a specific time. We discuss two models: the first is an extension of the classical Vasicek model, where the volatility term remains constant until a future time instant, where it starts to decrease. This model is then integrated into a regime-switching framework, where the perceived deadline for transitioning to a low or zero carbon economy defines the regime. Both models are calibrated using market data extracted from twin German government bonds. Empirical results suggest that recently, the market perceives a deceleration in the pace of transition.

title: The Entropic System, The Thermodynamics of Coordination, Decay, and Resilience

detail.title: The Entropic System, The Thermodynamics of Coordination, Decay, and Resilience
detail.abstract:
Standard organizational theory models institutions as static "machines" designed to solve specific coordination problems. This monograph argues that institutions are, instead, dynamic dissipative structures subject to the laws of thermodynamics. We introduce the Scale-Time-Failure (STF) Principle, a unified mathematical framework demonstrating that institutional decay is not a moral failing but a topological inevitability. By applying Reliability Engineering to the bureaucratic lattice, we derive a Weibull hazard function showing that "Sclerosis" scales non-linearly with system size (n) and duration (t). We demonstrate that efficiency-seeking agents naturally form Scale-Free network topologies, creating a "Paradox of Efficiency" where the formation of Hubs minimizes transaction costs but drives the system’s percolation threshold to zero.

Moving to the continuum limit, we model inequality not as a scalar metric but as a vector field, distinguishing between Tensile Stress (Innovation) and Shear Stress (Rent-Seeking). We show that systems dominated by shear stress possess a "Movable Singularity"—a finite-time rupture point determined by the accumulation of entropic waste. Finally, we apply Control Theory to the restoration problem, proving that continuous reform is mathematically incapable of stabilizing an entropic system. We conclude that resilience requires a discontinuous Reset Function; a "Sawtooth Strategy" of periodic, controlled de-scaling to prevent catastrophic rupture.

title: Modern Slavery and the Moral Allocation Problem: Why the World's Most Widespread Atrocity Remains Structurally Marginal

detail.title: Modern Slavery and the Moral Allocation Problem: Why the World's Most Widespread Atrocity Remains Structurally Marginal
detail.abstract: Modern slavery affects tens of millions of people worldwide and generates hundreds of billions of dollars in illicit economic activity annually. Despite its scale, persistence, and unequivocal prohibition under international law, it occupies a marginal position in contemporary moral, media, and institutional prioritization compared to more episodic atrocities such as genocide. This paper introduces the concept of the moral allocation problem: a structural mechanism by which moral attention, urgency, and enforcement are distributed according to narrative simplicity, political utility, and distance from economic self-implication rather than aggregate harm. Using comparative institutional analysis, secondary empirical data, and cross-disciplinary scholarship, the paper demonstrates that modern slavery is deprioritized not because it is ambiguous or unknown, but because confronting it would implicate global economic systems, consumer participation, and elite interests. The result is a paradoxical moral order in which the most prevalent atrocity is universally condemned yet structurally deferred.

title: Markowitz's Portfolio Variance Describes Only a Limited Case of Constant Trade Volumes
