detail.title: Strategic Interactions and Gender Cues: Evidence from Social Preference Games

publicationDetails.journalName: Inter-American Development Bank Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper studies trust, reciprocity, and bargaining using a large-scale online experi- ment conducted in six Latin American countries. Participants played trust and ultima- tum games under randomly assigned conditions in which the gender of their counterpart was either disclosed or withheld. On average, disclosing counterpart gender does not yield statistically detectable eects in either game. However, statistically signi cant dierences emerge by participants' own gender: on average men exhibit higher levels of trust, reciprocity, and generosity in bargaining than women. When disaggregating by participant{counterpart gender pairings, point estimates dier in sign across groups but are generally imprecisely estimated, and dierences between interacting with male versus female counterparts are generally not statistically distinguishable. Overall, the results are consistent with limited behavioral responses to counterpart gender when gender is conveyed through minimal, text-based cues, notwithstanding clear average gender dierences.

title: Strategic Leadership in AI-Enhanced Aviation: Balancing Financial and Environmental Goals through Differentiated Search
affiliations: University of Religions and Denominations and Islamic Azad University

detail.title: Strategic Leadership in AI-Enhanced Aviation: Balancing Financial and Environmental Goals through Differentiated Search
detail.abstract: This study examines how strategic leadership styles shape the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in airline operations, highlighting both financial performance and sustainability outcomes. A mixed-method design was employed, combining semi-structured interviews, archival operational reports, and document analyses of AI initiatives. Central to this research are multi-objective optimization algorithms including evolutionary computing and reinforcement learning that simultaneously improve cost-effectiveness and reduce environmental impacts. The findings show that transformational leadership fosters broad AI adoption, notably in areas like predictive maintenance and emission reduction, whereas transactional leadership tends to emphasize short-term efficiency gains. Quantitatively, evolutionary algorithms and reinforcement learning consistently produce cost reductions of 7-12% while yielding fuel savings of 6-10%, underscoring their potential to balance profitability with ecological responsibility. From a theoretical standpoint, these insights enrich leadership and digital transformation frameworks by illustrating how executive behaviors and complex AI technologies interact to achieve dual financial and environmental benefits. In practical terms, the study recommends forming cross-functional governance committees, enhancing leadership training to encourage visionary communication, and adopting phased AI deployments to manage elevated risk tolerance. To operationalize these findings, Appendix A provides a set of role-based Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for financial performance and sustainability, offering practitioners a clear metric framework for measuring progress. Overall, this research underscores the need to align AI-driven analytics with strategic leadership competencies and robust oversight mechanisms, presenting a roadmap to optimize costs, meet sustainability targets, and ensure resilient decision-making in the ever-evolving aviation sector.

title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Diagnostic Healthcare
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Diagnostic Healthcare

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: The immediate adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) into diagnostic healthcare has become an urgent solution to the longstanding global malabsorption of diagnostic accuracy, timeliness, and resource decisions, especially in strained health systems (Panesar, 2019; Ahmed et al., 2020). This research paper conducts a critical and systematic review of multidisciplinary sources encompassing clinical medicine, data science, health policy, and ethics in order to evaluate the potential and drawbacks of AI-powered diagnostic tools in terms of transformative power. Based on empirical, as well as conceptual evidence, the review establishes the gains in diagnostic accuracy, early disease diagnosis, and clinical decision support, and significant improvement has been shown across imaging, pathology, and predictive analytics (Undru et al., 2022; Mahalingam et al., 2024). Besides performance improvement, AI and MLs are also shown to have considerable workflow efficiencies in the sense that they minimize the burden on clinicians, facilitate real-time risk stratification, and facilitate individualized diagnostic pathways depending on patient profiles. Nevertheless, the synthesis also shows that there are still significant issues that inhibit massive and fair implementation, such as data bias, less explain ability, infrastructural differences, regulatory fragmentation, and ethical questions of accountability and patient trust. The main finding of the research is that AI and ML can significantly improve the diagnostic potential; however, their further usefulness is subject to responsible and human-centered integration that can synchronize technological advancement with clinical practice, ethical regulation of AI, and the design of health systems to be inclusive (Kudina and de Boer, 2021). These limitations need to be mitigated to make sure that AI-enabled diagnostics make a valuable contribution to health equity and system resilience across the globe.

title: Shadow P&L: Integrating Jungian Archetypes, Corporate Finance, and Gamification for Organizational Health

detail.title: Shadow P&L: Integrating Jungian Archetypes, Corporate Finance, and Gamification for Organizational Health
detail.abstract:
This working paper introduces the "Shadow P&L" framework—a novel diagnostic methodology that maps specific profit-and-loss line items to psychological shadow archetypes of company founders, particularly for mid-sized businesses ($30-50M revenue) navigating the critical "valley of death" growth phase.

Traditional financial analysis treats P&L anomalies (high CAC, bloated payroll, excessive R&D) as isolated operational failures requiring technical fixes. We propose that these financial pathologies are behavioral artifacts—crystallized manifestations of founders' unintegrated psychological patterns. Drawing on Jungian psychology, we identify four shadow archetypes: (1) The Hero's Shadow (Martyr/Bully) driving CAC inflation and high customer churn; (2) The Caregiver's Shadow (Enabler) creating payroll bloat and low revenue-per-employee; (3) The Creator's Shadow (Perfectionist) causing endless R&D cycles and feature creep; (4) The Ruler's Shadow (Tyrant) inflating administrative costs through micromanagement.

We validate this framework through cross-analysis of 100+ academic studies (including PNAS research showing founder personality predicts startup success 5x better than industry sector) and real-world case studies (Casper's CAC crisis, Apple's 11-year perfectionism stagnation, Tesla's 17-year burn rate). Our evidence demonstrates quantifiable correlations: narcissistic CEOs increase bankruptcy risk by 23%; perfectionism reduces growth rates by 23%; 15% payroll inefficiency eliminates net profit entirely.

The paper's distinctive contribution lies in prescribing "Gamification-as-Therapy"—twelve behavioral design interventions that redirect founders' shadow impulses into constructive organizational mechanics. These include: Client Tamagotchi (transforming Hero's conquest addiction into retention focus), Lifeboat Wargaming (training Caregiver's resource triage), Feature Tax (visualizing Creator's opportunity cost), and Autonomy Tree (delegating Ruler's control through leveling systems).

This framework offers practitioners a psychometric lens for P&L diagnostics, moving beyond spreadsheet optimization to address the root behavioral drivers of financial dysfunction. It also contributes to entrepreneurship research by operationalizing Jungian archetypes within corporate finance contexts—a previously unexplored interdisciplinary synthesis.

title: From Tools to Teammates: A Framework for Integrating AI Agents into Organizational Structures

detail.title: From Tools to Teammates: A Framework for Integrating AI Agents into Organizational Structures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a co‑founder of DialogAI, whose deployments are discussed as case examples in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable (no human subjects or sensitive data were involved).

detail.abstract:
Autonomous AI agents are increasingly deployed not just as productivity tools but as quasi‑members of organizational teams. Companies report that AI agents now draft software pull requests, resolve customer inquiries, qualify leads, and co‑create onboarding plans alongside human colleagues. Yet most management and information systems research still conceptualizes AI primarily as decision support or infrastructure, rather than as an organizational actor.

This working paper proposes a Three‑Level Maturity Framework for AI integration: Level 1 – AI as Tool, Level 2 – AI as Teammate, and Level 3 – AI as Workforce. The framework is grounded in public case evidence from software development, customer service, sales, marketing, and HR, combined with field observations from DialogAI deployments in customer‑facing environments and the author’s experience operating DialogAI as an “AI‑first” organization. A new metric, the Human–Agent Ratio (HAR), is introduced to quantify the depth of AI integration.

Findings suggest that most innovative organizations currently operate at Level 2, with AI agents performing roughly 40–60% of routine work in hybrid teams while humans focus on complex, relational, and strategic tasks. Customer‑facing scenarios introduce distinct challenges around trust, brand voice, and liability compared to internal use cases. The paper outlines practical design patterns for handoffs between humans and AI agents and identifies organizational readiness factors for moving beyond tool‑level adoption.

detail.title: Reforming the Automotive Regulatory Framework in Bangladesh: A Data-Driven Approach to Taxation, Modification, and Sustainability
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the systemic inefficiencies within Bangladesh's automotive sector, specifically focusing on the outdated Motor Vehicle Ordinance of 1983. Despite significant global advancements in vehicle safety, engine efficiency, and electric vehicle (EV) technology, the current regulatory framework remains anchored in engine-capacity-based taxation and restrictive modification laws that hinder economic growth and citizen welfare. Drawing on a primary survey of 222 automotive stakeholders and enthusiasts, this study identifies a high level of dissatisfaction with the current Advance Income Tax (AIT) structure and the lack of depreciation-based taxation. Findings reveal that 76% of respondents feel restricted by current modification laws, often leading to law enforcement challenges. This paper proposes a comprehensive reform package, including a power-based (kW) taxation slab , an age-discounted AIT model , and a framework for the regularization of vehicle modifications based on safety and environmental impact. The proposed reforms aim to stimulate the adoption of low-emission vehicles while creating a more transparent and modern bureaucratic environment for vehicle owners.

detail.abstract: Vendor compliance and retail standardization have become defining structural forces in the U.S. consumer market, fundamentally reshaping how consumer goods firms are managed and scaled. Large retailers increasingly impose standardized operational, logistical, and reporting requirements on vendors, extending their governance influence deep into supplier organizations. While these standards are often framed as efficiency-enhancing mechanisms, they introduce significant managerial, organizational, and strategic implications that remain underexplored in the business management literature. This paper examines the business management implications of vendor compliance and retail standardization, focusing on how standardized retail governance affects managerial decision-making, organizational design, and operational flexibility within consumer goods firms. Drawing on management, governance, and organizational control perspectives, the study develops a conceptual framework that explains how compliance requirements function not merely as operational constraints but as de facto governance mechanisms shaping firm behavior. The analysis highlights that vendor compliance generates both costs and strategic opportunities. While compliance imposes additional coordination burdens, resource allocation pressures, and risk exposure, it can also serve as a catalyst for managerial professionalization, internal control development, and organizational scalability. Firms that treat compliance reactively often experience strategic rigidity, whereas those that integrate compliance into core management systems are better positioned to convert standardization into a source of competitive advantage. By reframing vendor compliance as a central business management issue rather than a purely operational concern, this study contributes to a deeper understanding of retail governance in the U.S. consumer market. The findings offer actionable insights for executives navigating standardized retail environments and advance theoretical discussion on the intersection of governance, control, and strategy in contemporary consumer goods firms.

declarations.funderStatement: The author, Melisa Diaz Lema received funding from the Horizon Europe Framework (BRIDGE project, grant agreement number 101177154).

detail.abstract: Internationalization is widely promoted in higher education, yet it may entail tradeoffs for native students. While greater diversity can enhance the educational experience, changes in peer composition may reduce learning quality when students differ in cultural and academic backgrounds. This paper examines the effects of internationalization on the academic outcomes of native students. Using administrative panel data from a large public STEM university in Italy, we follow over 33,000 students across 17 programs and six cohorts. We exploit the introduction of an English parallel track in Civil Engineering using an instrumented difference-indifferences approach. The English track more than doubled the share of foreign students in the Civil Engineering program relative to the other primarily Italian-taught programs. We then examine the overall effect of expanding the English track and find that native students, regardless of whether they enroll in the Italian or English track, are less likely to drop out and more likely to graduate on time, although they achieve a slightly lower GPA. Further analysis of mechanisms reveals that international student inflows drive graduation gains, while larger classes and other changes to the learning environment explain the GPA decline. Our findings indicate that internationalization policies can improve native students' persistence and timely degree completion in higher education.

title: Innovation Acceleration Toolkit Hong Kong as a Focal Case: A Toolkit for Diagnosing and Accelerating Innovation Ecosystems

detail.title: Innovation Acceleration Toolkit Hong Kong as a Focal Case: A Toolkit for Diagnosing and Accelerating Innovation Ecosystems
detail.abstract: Innovation ecosystems often underperform not because of insufficient resources, but because actors lack a shared diagnostic framework for interpreting bottlenecks, aligning incentives, and sequencing interventions. This working paper introduces the Innovation Acceleration Toolkit, a three-part method designed to support ecosystem diagnosis and coordinated action. The Toolkit combines the Innovation Pentagon Model (for system mapping), the Innovation Maturity Model (for capability and integration assessment), and the Innovation Acceleration Canvas (for translating diagnosis into actionable strategies). To illustrate the Toolkit's application, Hong Kong is used as a focal case, integrating insights from expert interviews, ecosystem data, and comparative analysis. Findings highlight structural challenges related to commercialization pathways, early-stage financing, talent retention, and institutional coordination. While Hong Kong provides the empirical demonstration, the Toolkit is generalizable and intended for broader use across innovation ecosystems seeking to improve translational capacity and research-to-market outcomes. The contribution of this work lies in offering a practical, practitioner-oriented method for diagnosing innovation bottlenecks and designing ecosystemlevel interventions.

title: Apology for Vulcan: Precautionary Objections and the Moral Duty of Liberal Defence

detail.title: Apology for Vulcan: Precautionary Objections and the Moral Duty of Liberal Defence
detail.abstract: Debates over autonomous weapon systems (AWS) and other emerging military technologies often rely on precautionary reasoning: uncertain but potentially grave risks are taken to justify prohibition or moratoria. This paper argues that such reasoning, even in its most sophisticated reconstructions, conducts one-sided moral accounting. Precautionary frameworks treat restraint as a neutral baseline and catalogue development risks while systematically neglecting the positive obligations liberal democratic states bear toward those they govern and defend. From a Walzerian non-ideal standpoint, liberal democracies possess duties to protect citizens, uphold alliances, and preserve the institutional conditions of liberty—duties that require maintaining effective military power under conditions of partial compliance and strategic competition. Effectiveness demands not merely symbolic defense but credible capability, which depends on sustained technological competence and active research and development of emerging capabilities. These developmental duties generate presumptive reasons to pursue emerging military technologies rather than unilaterally forgoing them, though they remain constrained by precautionary concerns and by requirements that military development not undermine liberal institutions themselves. The resulting framework rejects both technological maximalism and categorical restraint, establishing that both development and prohibition constitute morally significant choices requiring justification against standing obligations. The tension between defensive duties and liberal constraints represents an irreducible moral dilemma requiring practical judgment rather than algorithmic resolution. The contribution is methodological: by exposing how precautionary objections ignore half the moral landscape, this analysis forces recognition that liberal states face genuine tragic choices in military technology development where all options carry moral costs and neither side succeeds merely by cataloguing risks of alternatives.

The other point was to see whether the household's attitude affected the relationship between these two variables. That is, to see if household attitude played a moderating role between food waste and food insecurity. A survey was therefore carried out on a sample of 272 people, using a questionnaire. detail.abstract:
Subterranean infrastructure ranging from military tunnel networks to hardened underground logistics hubs has emerged as a critical domain of modern conflict, enabling concealment, survivability, and strategic maneuver below the threshold of traditional surveillance. This paper presents a comprehensive technical and operational evaluation of a next-generation AI-fused subterranean domain awareness architecture designed to detect, characterize, and monitor underground activity under diverse geological and urban conditions.

The proposed approach integrates heterogeneous sensing modalities including ground-penetrating radar (GPR), seismic and acoustic sensing, interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR), and limited electromagnetic measurements through early fusion using cross-modal transformer architectures. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are employed to embed governing physical constraints directly into inference, enabling robust reconstruction and anomaly detection in environments characterized by sparse labels, high noise, and strong material attenuation. Performance targets, sensor density, and detection confidence are explicitly conditioned on subsurface conductivity and soil composition, reflecting fundamental physical limits rather than idealized assumptions.

The paper evaluates system architecture, edge-compute feasibility, operational concepts, validation pathways, and governance considerations, including human-on-the-loop constraints for operational decision-making. Drawing on open-source intelligence and recent operational disclosures, representative case studies illustrate the scale, depth, and survivability characteristics of contemporary tunnel networks while maintaining appropriate epistemic caution.

The results demonstrate a technically viable and operationally realistic pathway to reducing subterranean opacity, while clearly identifying limitations, failure modes, and research gaps. This work is intended as an unclassified technical assessment to inform future research, experimentation, and requirements development in subterranean sensing and counter-tunnel operations.

title: Geopolitics in the Courtroom: How AIIB Membership Shapes Cross-Border Patent Disputes in China
affiliations: ESSEC Business School, Tsinghua univeristy and IESE Business School

detail.title: Geopolitics in the Courtroom: How AIIB Membership Shapes Cross-Border Patent Disputes in China
detail.abstract: In the knowledge economy, intellectual-property litigation has become central to corporate strategy, with multinational enterprises depending on global legal actions to protect their technological edge. Yet, due to the rising nationalisms and geopolitical tensions, the courts that adjudicate these disputes are unlikely to represent neutral venues. We argue that, in a multipolar world, foreign firms are not treated uniformly: judicial outcomes pivot on the signals of alignment litigants' home countries send to the forum state. To test this claim, we investigate how a country's decision to join the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB)-a China-led multilateral development bank that epitomizes Beijing's efforts to reshape global financial institutions-shapes the legal treatment of its firms when they initiate patent suits in Chinese courts. Specifically, we estimate a difference-indifferences model on patent lawsuits filed by foreign subsidiaries in China between 2010 and 2020. Our findings reveal strong evidence that plaintiff firms from AIIB member countries experience systematically more favorable rulings in Chinese courts during patent disputes, suggesting that judicial decisionmaking aligns with China's broader geopolitical and economic strategies.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in Human Resource Management (HRM), reshaping traditional HR functions and redefining the strategic role of HR professionals. In the Indian corporate context, AI adoption in HRM has gained momentum due to the need for efficiency, fairness, scalability, and employee-centric practices. This article examines the role of AI in transforming key HR functions such as recruitment and talent acquisition, employee engagement, learning and development, performance management, employee retention, diversity and inclusion, payroll, and compliance. Drawing upon practical examples from leading Indian organizations such as Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, and ICICI Bank, the study highlights how AI enhances decision-making, reduces bias, and enables predictive and personalized HR practices. The article also discusses the challenges associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, high implementation costs, and the need for continuous upskilling of HR professionals. The study concludes that AI is shifting HRM in India from an administrative support function to a strategic, value-driven organizational role.
